\paragraph{Exact repair on natural score graphs.}
A second, prospectively fixed diagnostic applied the unchanged indexed
repair algorithm to the same 1,001 records at all 51 cutoffs. It maintained
exact integer membership coordinates rather than a task learner. One
fixed record-deletion sequence and one contributor-proxy source-deletion
sequence were reused across cuts, each with a horizon of 128 requests.
All 13,056 singleton updates matched a direct raw-blocker membership
oracle. At 408 checkpoints, after $1,8,32,128$ requests per sequence,
sequential, batch and reverse-order updates had exactly equal logical
coefficient and index states; recomputing the retained-data graph and
reconstructing the state at the remaining horizon agreed as well.
An independent aggregate audit checked the bound execution receipts;
private-state equality was tested within the cluster run.
This checks exact repair for these development cases. It does not certify
physical byte equality or erasure, enforce a no-reaccess boundary, or
establish learner accuracy, semantic usefulness, speedup or memory savings.
The failed calibration gates and original evaluation reservations remain
unchanged.

\paragraph{Theory and software evidence.}

The separate repair diagnostic completed in 1,193.413 seconds, with
281,616,384 bytes of process peak RSS, reusing the existing embedding
cache. It requested two CPUs and no GPU, with one numerical thread.
These figures cover this diagnostic and its checks; they are not a
comparative service benchmark or the cost of the complete pipeline.

Literature coverage is also bounded.
